# Standard widgets

Import them from `std-widgets.zge`:

```
import { Button, LineEdit, Palette } from "std-widgets.zge";
```

They are written in `.zge` ([src/widgets](../../src/widgets)) and come
in three styles, chosen at build time: `fluent` (the default),
`material` and `minimal`. The style changes their look (the `Palette`
colors and `Style` sizes), not their properties. Besides the
properties listed here, each has those of the element it inherits,
and those of every element: `visible` and `enabled` among them
(disabled, a widget greys itself and takes no input).

## Button

Inherits `Rectangle`. A push button. `primary` uses the accent color. Space or Return clicks it when it has keyboard focus.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | in |  |  |
| `primary` | bool | in |  |  |
| `pressed` | bool | out |  |  |
| `has-hover` | bool | out |  |  |
| `has-focus` | bool | out |  |  |

Callbacks:

- `clicked()`

## ListView

Inherits `ScrollView`. A vertical list in a ScrollView: `ListView { for item in model : Row {} }`. The rows are all as tall as the first (or `row-height`), or, with `variable-row-height`, each as tall as it is (those not yet shown estimated at the mean of those that were), and only those in view have instances: scrolling hands them on to the rows coming in (with their own state, a text typed in one, say). `sections` names each row's section: one starts, under its header, where the name changes; the header of the section at the top stays pinned there.

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `row-height` | length | in |  |  |
| `variable-row-height` | bool | in |  |  |
| `spacing` | length | in |  |  |
| `sections` | [string] | in |  |  |
| `section-height` | length | in | `28px` |  |
| `count` | int | out |  |  |
| `current-section` | string | out |  |  |

## StandardListView

Inherits `ScrollView`. A scrolling list of strings with a current item. The up and down arrow keys move it when the list has focus. With `selection-mode: extended`, the user selects several items as on desktops (Ctrl- or Cmd-click adds or removes one, Shift-click or Shift and the arrows a range, Ctrl+A or Cmd+A all); with `multiple`, each click (or Space) adds or removes one. `selected-items` are the items selected (in `single` mode, the current one).

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | [string] | in |  |  |
| `current-item` | int | in-out | `-1` |  |
| `selection-mode` | SelectionMode | in | `single` |  |
| `selected-items` | [int] | out |  |  |

Callbacks:

- `current-item-changed(int)`: Called when the user makes an item current.
- `selection-changed()`: Called when the items selected change.

Functions:

- `set-current-item(i: int)`
- `select-all()`
- `clear-selection()`
- `set-selected(i: int, on: bool)`

## StandardTableView

Inherits `Rectangle`. A table of strings: `columns` are the headers, `rows` the cells. Columns share the width unless `column-widths` gives theirs. Clicking a header asks the app to sort by it; the up and down arrows move the current row. With `selection-mode: extended`, the user selects several rows as on desktops (Ctrl- or Cmd-click adds or removes one, Shift-click or Shift and the arrows a range, Ctrl+A or Cmd+A all); with `multiple`, each click (or Space) adds or removes one. `selected-rows` are the rows selected (in `single` mode, the current one). Screen readers see a table: the headers (sorting when pressed), then the rows (selected when pressed), each with its cells.

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` | [string] | in |  |  |
| `rows` | [[string]] | in |  |  |
| `column-widths` | [length] | in |  |  |
| `current-row` | int | in-out | `-1` |  |
| `selection-mode` | SelectionMode | in | `single` |  |
| `selected-rows` | [int] | out |  |  |
| `sort-column` | int | out |  |  |
| `sort-ascending` | bool | out |  |  |

Callbacks:

- `current-row-changed(int)`: Called when the user makes a row current.
- `selection-changed()`: Called when the rows selected change.
- `sort-requested(int, bool)`: Called when a header is clicked: sort the rows by that column.

Functions:

- `set-current-row(r: int)`
- `select-all()`
- `clear-selection()`
- `set-selected(r: int, on: bool)`
- `column-width(c: int) -> length`
- `column-x(c: int) -> length`

## TableView

Inherits `Rectangle`. A table whose rows are yours: `TableView { columns: ["Name", "Born"]; for p in people : TableRow { Text { text: p.name; } Text { ... } } }`. Each child of a TableRow is a cell, in its column; columns share the width unless `column-widths` gives theirs. Rows are `row-height` tall (0: as tall as the first's tallest cell), and only those in view have instances, handed on as it scrolls (as in a ListView). Clicking a header asks the app to sort by it.

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |

| `column-widths` | [length] | in |  |  |
| `row-height` | length | in | `32px` |  |
| `viewport-y` | length | in-out |  |  |
| `visible-height` | length | out |  |  |
| `row-count` | int | out |  |  |
| `sort-column` | int | out |  |  |
| `sort-ascending` | bool | out |  |  |

Callbacks:

- `sort-requested(int, bool)`: Called when a header is clicked: sort the rows by that column.

Functions:

- `column-width(c: int) -> length`
- `column-x(c: int) -> length`

## Sound

Inherits `Audio`. A sound effect: `jump.play()` plays it again from the start, over the voices still playing (up to `voices`).

## Music

Inherits `Audio`. Music: loops, rises over `fade-in` when it starts and falls over `fade-out` when it stops. A new `source` fades in while the old one fades out.

## VideoPlayer

Inherits `Rectangle`. A video with controls: play and pause (the button, or a click on the picture), the time, and a bar to seek with (the picture follows the pointer while dragging; it plays on from where it is let go, if it was playing). The controls stay while paused or pointed at, and hide while it plays.

| `position` | duration | out |  |  |
| `duration` | duration | out |  |  |

## ToolTip

Inherits `PopupWindow`. A hint shown when the pointer rests on something: put it in the element and bind `shown` to the hover (`shown: area.has-hover`). It appears after `delay`, above the element (kept in the window), and takes no input: clicks go to what is under it.

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | in |  |  |
| `shown` | bool | in |  | Whether it should show (it does after `delay`). |
| `delay` | duration | in | `700ms` |  |

## Menu

Inherits `PopupWindow`. A popup list of actions: a context menu (`open-at(x, y)`, from a TouchArea's `right-clicked`), or the menu of a button or a menu bar. Hover or the arrow keys highlight an item; a click, Return or Space chooses it (`activated(index)`, its index in `items`) and closes the menu; Escape or a click outside closes it. An entry with a submenu opens it beside it (hovered, clicked, or with Right, Return or Space; Left closes it), on the other side if there is no room. It stays in the window.

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | [MenuItem] | in |  |  |

Callbacks:

- `activated(int)`: The item chosen.

Functions:

- `open-at(x: length, y: length)`: Opens it at `x`, `y` in its parent (where a right click was, say).
- `open()`: Opens it where it is (not while disabled).

## Dialog

Inherits `PopupWindow`. A modal dialog: `open()` shows it over the whole window (dimmed), and the rest of the window takes no input until it closes. Its content is the elements put in it, under `heading`; `buttons` are its buttons, right to left from the last. Return presses the default button (`accepted`), Escape the cancel one (`rejected`); each button calls `clicked(index)` and closes the dialog. Tab moves the focus among its controls only.

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `heading` | string | in |  |  |
| `buttons` | [string] | in | `["OK"]` |  |
| `default-button` | int | in | `root.buttons.length - 1` | The button Return presses (drawn as the primary one), and the one Escape does (-1: none, Escape only closes). |
| `cancel-button` | int | in | `-1` |  |
| `panel-width` | length | in | `400px` | The panel's width (its height follows the content). |

Callbacks:

- `clicked(int)`
- `accepted()`: The default button, or the cancel one (or Escape), was chosen.
- `rejected()`

Functions:

- `open()`
- `choose(i: int)`: Closes it as if the button `i` was chosen.

Inherits `Empty`. A radio button: one choice of several. A click (or Space, with keyboard focus) checks it; checking another one of the group is its owner's job (bind `checked`, or use a ButtonGroup). `toggled` comes first: when the owner's handler makes a binding of `checked` true, the binding stays (so the button unchecks when another is chosen); only otherwise is `checked` set.

## TreeView

Inherits `ScrollView`. A scrolling tree: its rows (`model`, in order, with their depths), those under collapsed ones hidden, and a current one (`current-item`, a row of the model). A click on an arrow expands or collapses; on a row, makes it current. With the keyboard: Up and Down move, Right expands (or goes to the first child), Left collapses (or goes to the parent), Space or Return toggles. With `selection-mode: extended`, the user selects several rows as on desktops (Ctrl- or Cmd-click adds or removes one, Shift-click or Shift and Up or Down the rows shown between, Ctrl+A or Cmd+A all); with `multiple`, each click adds or removes one. In both, Space adds or removes the current row (Return still toggles). `selected-items` are the rows selected (in `single` mode, the current one).

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | [TreeItem] | in |  |  |
| `initially-expanded` | bool | in |  |  |
| `current-item` | int | in-out | `-1` |  |
| `selection-mode` | SelectionMode | in | `single` |  |
| `selected-items` | [int] | out |  |  |

Callbacks:

- `current-item-changed(int)`: Called when the user makes a row current.
- `selection-changed()`: Called when the rows selected change.

Functions:

- `expand-all()`
- `collapse-all()`
- `toggle(row: int)`
- `select-all()`
- `clear-selection()`
- `set-selected(row: int, on: bool)`

## Drawer

Inherits `PopupWindow`. A panel that slides in from an edge of the window (`edge`), over the window dimmed: `open()` shows it, `dismiss()` slides it out (so do a click on the dimmed window, a swipe towards its edge, and Escape). With `interactive`, it is also pulled out by a drag from that edge of the window (begun within `drag-margin` of it): let go past half way, or flicked, it opens, else it slides back. Its content is the elements put in it, one above the other. `size` is its width (its height from the top or bottom).

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `edge` | DrawerEdge | in | `DrawerEdge.left` |  |
| `size` | length | in | `280px` |  |
| `interactive` | bool | in | `true` |  |
| `drag-margin` | length | in | `20px` |  |
| `position` | float | out |  | How far it is in (0: out, 1: in). |

Callbacks:

- `dismissed()`: It went (slid out, or Escape).

Functions:

- `open()`
- `dismiss()`

## VirtualKeyboard

Inherits `Rectangle`. An on-screen keyboard, for touch screens without a physical one (KMS, microcontrollers). It types into the focused text input and is open only while one can be typed into (or `always-open`): put it at the bottom of the window's layout, where it takes no room while closed. Letters (Shift once for a capital, twice to lock), digits and symbols (?123, then =\<), Backspace (held: it repeats), space and Return. The key at the bottom right closes it, taking the focus away.

| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `always-open` | bool | in |  |  |
| `key-height` | length | in | `44px` | The height of a key. |
| `spacing` | length | in | `6px` |  |
| `open` | bool | out |  |  |

## Style

A global: use its properties as `Style.name`.


| Property | Type | Access | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `font-size` | length | out | `14px` | Text. |
| `control-height` | length | out | `32px` | Buttons, combo boxes, spin boxes, line edits. |
| `control-radius` | length | out | `4px` |  |
| `button-radius` | length | out | `4px` |  |
| `button-border-width` | length | out | `1px` |  |
| `focus-ring-width` | length | out | `2px` | The focus ring: its width and distance from the control. |
| `focus-ring-offset` | length | out | `3px` |  |
| `input-border-width` | length | out | `1px` | Text fields: border, and an accent underline when focused (0: none). |
| `input-focus-border-width` | length | out | `1px` |  |
| `input-underline` | length | out | `2px` |  |
| `check-size` | length | out | `20px` | Check boxes. |
| `check-radius` | length | out | `4px` |  |
| `check-border-width` | length | out | `1px` |  |
| `switch-width` | length | out | `40px` | Switches: the track, and the knob when off, on, hovered. |
| `switch-height` | length | out | `20px` |  |
| `switch-radius` | length | out | `10px` |  |
| `switch-border-width` | length | out | `1px` |  |
| `switch-knob-off` | length | out | `12px` |  |
| `switch-knob-on` | length | out | `12px` |  |
| `switch-knob-grow` | length | out | `2px` |  |
| `slider-track` | length | out | `4px` | Sliders: track, thumb and the dot in it. |
| `slider-thumb` | length | out | `20px` |  |
| `slider-thumb-border-width` | length | out | `1px` |  |
| `slider-dot` | length | out | `12px` |  |
| `progress-height` | length | out | `4px` | Progress bars: their height, the track line and the bar. |
| `progress-track` | length | out | `1px` |  |
| `progress-bar` | length | out | `3px` |  |
| `control-shadow-y` | length | out | `1px` | Shadows under buttons, combo boxes and check boxes (fluent: a darker bottom edge), and under switch knobs and slider thumbs. |
| `control-shadow-blur` | length | out | `0px` |  |
| `knob-shadow-y` | length | out | `0px` |  |
| `knob-shadow-blur` | length | out | `0px` |  |
| `popup-radius` | length | out | `6px` | Popups, cards and tabs. |
| `card-radius` | length | out | `8px` |  |
| `tab-indicator-width` | length | out | `16px` | The selected tab's indicator (0: the tab's whole width). |
